belief: If I'm not productive, I'm wasting the life God gave me.
origins: Productivity can become a moral standard. Lists, goals, and income can turn into a daily scoreboard. Every unproductive hour can seem like a failure, and illness, caregiving, unemployment, or old age can feel like waste. Many of us were praised when we achieved and ignored when we rested.
teaches: The psalmist prays, “So teach us to number our days, that we may present a heart of wisdom.” Paul says, “We are God’s workmanship, created in Christ Jesus to do good works, which God prepared in advance as our way of life,” so God prepares the works. When Martha was busy and worried, Jesus said, “only one thing is necessary. Mary has chosen the good portion.” God also says, “Be still and know that I am God.” A well-lived life is measured by wisdom, love, and presence, not output.
self_statements: Every unproductive minute is a waste.
Being sick means I am useless.
I am only valuable when I produce.
I will regret all the time I wasted.
errors: Insisting that I must always be productive.
Seeing time as either productive or wasted.
Treating rest or slow seasons as huge failures.
questions: Who taught me to measure life by output?
What do Scripture’s verses on wisdom say about how to number my days?
What did Jesus say about Mary’s choice?
What things in life matter that cannot be measured, such as love, prayer, or presence?
What is God doing in seasons when I cannot produce?
What would a good day look like that is not measured by tasks?
truth: My life is not measured by output. God prepared good works for me, and He also calls me to be still, to love, and to sit at His feet. A season of rest or slowness is not wasted in His hands.
hw_truths: God numbers my days with wisdom.
He prepared good works for me.
Sitting at His feet is the good portion.
No season is wasted in His hands.
log: Each day, write one unmeasured thing that mattered, such as a conversation, a prayer, or a moment outdoors.
actions: List how you measure a good day and who taught it.
Put time with God or a loved one on your list.
Spend 10 minutes in quiet with Psalm 46:10.
Note moments of love and kindness, not just tasks.
prayer: Lord, teach me to number my days with wisdom. Free me from measuring my worth by output. Help me sit at Your feet, do the works You prepared, and trust that no season is wasted. Amen.
hw_questions: Who taught me to measure life by output?
What matters that cannot be measured?
What would a good day look like?
What is God doing in slow seasons?
